title: PR CI path filters: TypeScript SDK and copilot-*.yml changes are in the pull_request paths-ignore of the Python, R and build workflows
answers: Why did a PR that only changes Copilot workflow files start the MLflow Python tests?
My TypeScript SDK-only PR is still running cross-version, tracing or examples CI. Which path filters control that?
Where is the pull_request paths-ignore for the R or fs2db workflow defined, and what does it skip?
Do push or scheduled runs still happen when only libs/typescript or copilot workflow files change?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/master.yml, build-wheel.yml, cross-version-tests.yml, examples.yml, fs2db.yml, r.yml, tracing.yml and typescript.yml. Each `pull_request` `paths-ignore` list decides whether a PR that touches only certain files starts the MLflow tests, cross-version tests, tracing, examples, fs2db, build-wheel, R or TypeScript workflow.
Rule: Each of those lists carries `libs/typescript/**` and `.github/workflows/typescript.yml` directly after `mlflow/server/js/**` and `.github/workflows/js.yml`. It also carries `.github/workflows/copilot-*.yml` immediately before `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, so Copilot workflow-file changes skip them without editing each list. Keep the `copilot-*.yml` glob so new Copilot workflow files are covered automatically. When a new non-Python subtree or workflow family should not start Python CI, add it to the same list in every PR-triggered workflow, not just one.
Symptom: TypeScript SDK-only pull requests started the unrelated MLflow Python test, cross-version, tracing, examples, fs2db, build-wheel and R workflows. Changes limited to `.github/workflows/copilot-*.yml` likewise started those unrelated workflows.
Constraints: Applies only to `pull_request` path filters. The `push`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers are unchanged, so those runs still happen. The TypeScript SDK workflow and the always-on lint workflows stay active. Mixed changes that touch any non-ignored path still run the Python workflows.
applies: Pull-request path filters (paths-ignore) in .github/workflows for Python, R, build and TypeScript-related CI; not push, schedule or manual triggers.

says: Pull requests touching only TypeScript code are triggering unnecessary Python automated test suites.
Modifying Copilot automation workflows unnecessarily triggers the entire Python validation pipeline.
Prevent TypeScript client pull requests from running packaging and wheel building jobs.
Pull requests updating only the client library waste build minutes running backend tests.
Skip execution of R and database test workflows when only client SDKs change.
